notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 9th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Tyler Bertuzzi is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. He is a top-six forward.
Patrick Kane is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is a top-six forward. Teuvo Teräväinen has taken his spot beside Frank Nazar and Oliver Moore.

Bowen Byram is on injured reserve (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 19 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 33% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 79:38 together, down from 47% with Byram.
Wyatt Kaiser is suspended and has missed the last 3 games. Ian Cole has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov.
Luke Glendening joined from NYR on Nov 23 and has played beside Jordan Greenway and Cole Smith.

story.head: The Blackhawks come in hot
paras: The Predators (13-6-6) lost 6-5 in a shootout to Utah on Friday, while the Blackhawks have won four straight. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Blackhawks last (tied for 27th in the NHL) and the Preds third (tied for ninth). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Blackhawks’ record (.423) is about what their chances are worth. The Predators’ record (.640) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.526), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games.

The Blackhawks get their shots through better than almost anyone (2nd), but don’t block many shots (31st). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Predators’ penalty killers. Chicago has allowed 3.73 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), get pinned in their own end on long shifts (30th) and give up a lot of shots (30th). The Predators get in close, but the Blackhawks mostly shoot from distance.

Roman Kantserov (15 G / 5 A / 20 P in 26 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Sam Rinzel (2 G / 16 A / 18 P in 25 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Predators, Filip Forsberg (10 G / 17 A / 27 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight goals in twelve games against Chicago since 2023-24. Steven Stamkos (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 25 GP) has a team-high twelve goals.
Spencer Knight (9-11-1 / .895 SV% in 21 GS) is in line to start for Chicago. Juuse Saros (9-4-5 / .914 SV% in 18 GS) has been a rock in net for Nashville and will likely start.
At home, Andrew Brunette likes to send Schaefer, Kerfoot and Marchessault out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Mangiapane, Greene and Boucher.
